T-3020: 1736 Prairie's card stops showing the other McBirney house (#1201)

* T-3020: 1736 Prairie's card stops showing the other McBirney house

The January 1890 Inland Architect plate "Residence for Hugh J. McBirney" is the
son's Tudor stone house at 1625 Prairie. Its library record still listed the
Art Institute's wrong catalogue address (1736) under addresses, and the library
places a record on every lot its addresses name, so the plate sat on 1736's
lot: at the top of 1736's card and in its structure grade. The address is
dropped (the notes keep why). The June 1889 American Architect permit for
H. J. McBirney's three-storey Burling & Whitehouse dwelling is the same 1625
house and moves there too. 1736's model was built from its own c. 1890
photograph and is unchanged.

Rebuilding images.json also folds in library edits other PRs left unbuilt:
the three 2013 Glessner capital close-ups (now with their evidence reviews and
image-store entries) and three Glessner record edits; site-plan.json
re-derives from the current street grid. Sidecar grades and the built-so-far
walk re-derive.

T-3021: Take the tour leads Guide; Inspect gets a magnifying glass; Home's tiles open Move and Confidence; Inspect's tabs pinned with Back (#1203)

The owner, 2026-10-22: the tour offer comes up once and then the tour
cannot be found; Home and Inspect both look like houses; the Move and
Confidence view tiles should go to those screens; and in a building's
view the tab row scrolls away with no way back.

- Guide lifts the field check's block (#guide-tour, its key still
  #tour-start) to the top of its screen: Take the tour, any time.
- Inspect's rail icon and the HUD's Inspect key are a magnifying glass.
- Home's MOVE and CONFIDENCE VIEW tiles are buttons opening those apps.
- Inspect's Back key and tabs ride one bar pinned to the top of the
  screen; the tabs wrap so Photos and Sources show at 400 px. Back goes
  to the app Inspect was opened from (navigator.backTo/back), else Home.

T-3017: 1904 parkway elms grow as open-grown American elms; leaf cards cut to their leaves (#1199)

The parkway elm drew as one straight bole under a round crown, and at the
street's mid level every leaf clump was one card of the massed-clump tile,
a fan of sprays, which the owner saw as "fans of leaves and not branches".

- tree-model.js: ARCH.ulmus_americana_vase and growElm: clear bole to about a
  third, 2-4 co-dominant stems that fork again and arch out, branches sweeping
  out and down, hanging twigs; leaf as sprays hung from the twigs and faced to
  the street and the ground; every child grows from its parent's wood.
- Every grown tree's leaf card is cut to its tile's opaque box (LEAF_CROP,
  printed by generate_tree_atlas.py --crops): same leaves in the same place,
  about 30% less card area for the GPU to shade and alpha-test.
- Phone tier (`coarse`): fewer, larger sprays and no sub-pixel branches; the
  phone's distant ring for the elms comes in to 220 m.
- Liberty L-elm-vase-3017, changelog entry.
